title: Intro to Claude
claims: The Anthropic platform presents API and SDK development separately from the Claude chat product.

The documented model interface accepts text, code, and image inputs; an application must supply its own agent loop, persistence, policy, and executor unless it uses a separate Anthropic product service.
notes: Product-family distinction only; this record makes no model-quality, pricing, or market-use claim.

title: Model Context Protocol
claims: Anthropic documents MCP as an open protocol for supplying context and tools to LLM applications.
The documentation identifies distinct MCP surfaces in the Messages API, Claude Code, Claude.ai, and Claude Desktop.
notes: MCP availability does not prove equivalent authentication, approval, locality, or execution behavior across product surfaces.

title: CLI reference
claims: Claude Code supports interactive CLI sessions plus print/programmatic modes, JSON or stream-JSON output, continuation/resume, MCP configuration, and selected permission/tool flags.
The CLI documents both bounded agentic turns and an explicit permission-bypass option.
notes: Terminal-agent details are covered in terminal-agents.md; this ledger retains only the product-surface boundary needed by this chapter.

title: Desktop application
claims: Claude Desktop has Chat, Cowork, and Code tabs; its Code surface supports local, remote-cloud, and SSH environments, panels, an integrated terminal, file/diff/preview views, and parallel sessions with Git isolation.
Remote Claude Code sessions can continue after the desktop app is closed; local sessions directly access the machine and SSH sessions run on the selected remote host.
Computer use is separately gated, disabled by default, and is broader than Bash or connector access; the desktop documentation also describes application-level approval and control categories.
notes: Feature and plan/platform availability are explicitly conditional; Desktop is documented for macOS and Windows, with CLI used on Linux.

title: Commands
claims: The command reference documents background sessions, subagent management, task listing, batch work in isolated worktrees, remote control, resume/branch, review, and PR-autofix commands.
Command availability can depend on platform, plan, and environment.
notes: This is a documented capability inventory, not evidence that every command is available to every account or that orchestration is reliable.

title: Automate work with scheduled tasks
claims: Claude Code documents scheduled routines that can run as cloud sessions or local desktop tasks.
Cloud routine runs have no permission-mode selector or in-run approval prompt; execution placement and permissions therefore need explicit operational review.
notes: Scheduling is an automation surface, not proof of durable workflow receipts, idempotency, or a general-purpose scheduler API.

title: Get started with Claude Cowork
claims: Cowork is an agentic-work surface distinct from Claude Code, with task/session work, global and folder instructions, plugins, connectors, browser actions, and recurring scheduled tasks.
Cowork documents Manual, Auto, and Skip approval behavior; Skip has no automatic action checks, while availability of automatic approval can be organization-controlled.
notes: The modes describe product behavior, not a claim that they provide an independently auditable per-effect policy ledger.

title: Use Claude Cowork on web, desktop, and mobile
claims: Cowork supports starting, steering, reviewing, and resuming tasks on desktop, web, and mobile; connectors, skills/plugins, projects, scheduled tasks, and current artifacts have documented surface-specific availability.

Web/mobile cloud sessions reach local files, local connectors, browser use, and computer use only through an open Claude Desktop app under stated session and folder conditions; a cloud task can continue without local-file reachability.
notes: Cowork in the cloud is documented as beta for some plans, and local-folder projects/local MCP features remain desktop-bound.

title: Use connectors to extend Claude's capabilities
claims: Connectors can retrieve data and take actions in connected services, with access bounded by the connected person's service permissions or by a custom connector's shared credential.
Anthropic documents connectors across Claude, Cowork, Claude Desktop, Claude mobile, Claude Code, and the API through the MCP Connector.
notes: Connector presence does not establish least privilege, action receipt retention, or an equivalent authorization model for custom credentials.

title: When to use desktop and web connectors
claims: Remote connectors are the cross-surface path for cloud/SaaS services, while desktop extensions serve local files, localhost, desktop applications, clipboard, and local processes.
Desktop extensions are limited to Claude Desktop and Claude Code; plugins can package remote and/or local MCP servers.
notes: This locality split is product documentation, not a claim that any arbitrary local service is safely exposed.

title: Use skills in Claude
claims: Skills are specialized knowledge/workflow packages; documented built-ins cover Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and PDF work, and custom skills can be uploaded as ZIP packages.
Skill availability is conditional on code execution/file creation and, for organizations, administrator policy.
notes: A skill is not an execution sandbox or a guarantee of document fidelity.

title: Use plugins in Claude
claims: Plugins bundle skills, connectors, and sub-agents; hooks and sub-agents are documented as Cowork-only while bundled skills can work in chat, Desktop Chat, and Cowork.
A plugin can include local MCP servers that execute on the computer with normal local-program permissions; enterprise controls and scanning can restrict installation.
notes: Plugins are proprietary-product behavior references only; do not reuse their implementation or treat scanning as a complete trust boundary.

title: What are projects?
claims: Projects provide workspaces with chat history, uploaded knowledge, and project instructions; paid plans may use RAG for larger project knowledge.

A new Projects version is documented as a staged beta beginning with some Claude Code users: it can run parallel cloud threads whose starting context includes the project's files, repositories, instructions, and memory.
notes: The staged rollout means Projects behavior must be capability-detected; no claim is made about universal rollout or persistent-memory correctness.

title: What are artifacts and how do I use them?
claims: Artifacts are editable/shareable outputs such as documents, decks, dashboards, designs, code, and small interactive tools; Claude Code can publish session output as a live artifact at a private URL.
Artifacts can use connected apps after first-use approval and can persist personal or shared text storage, subject to stated surface, plan, and storage limits.
notes: Artifact connector support excludes tools requiring approval for every action; sharing/storage choices create a separate data-handling boundary.

title: Use Claude Cowork on Team and Enterprise plans
claims: Cowork browser work can use the Claude Desktop built-in browser or the Claude in Chrome extension; each has organization controls, requirements, and documented safety checks.

Organization settings control automatic approval, write-capable connector always-allow behavior, plugins, and some browser access; the most restrictive relevant control wins for described Enterprise role grants.
notes: Organization controls are vendor-service configuration, not evidence of Splyce parity or a comprehensive external-service authorization proof.
